name: the Modern Age
summary: Asphalt, clear signage and leafy public space frame the Mayor's welcoming, everyday town.

rules.roads: Use smooth charcoal asphalt along x, 8 m wide within |z| <= 4. Street dressing: 26 low parts below 1.2 m, including flat white lane dashes, a short pedestrian crossing near a junction, flush drain grates, patched asphalt and simple margin bollards. Keep the central route free of raised obstructions; paint is surface-flat. Use crisp but sparse markings so the town remains readable.
rules.walkingEdge: Concrete slab pavements occupy |z| 4–6 with a consistent 0.12 m kerb, narrow gutters and lowered crossing points. Tree pits and fixtures sit at z 5 while leaving circulation around them. Use simple contemporary details, not Victorian railings or decorative cobbled frontage.
rules.lotMarkers: Free lot: 12 parts on a 16 m parcel, with a compact recycled panel on a square post near x 4.5, z 4.5. A large amber empty ring on a pale field provides the wordless available signal; optional small text must not carry the meaning. Add sparse grass and two gravel patches. Community lot: 16 parts, with four low corner blocks and a green municipal marker bearing four nodes around one shared centre, plus a simple building-hand pictogram. Keep the interior clear for collaborative construction.
rules.boundaries: Claimed lot: 28 parts including the owner marker. Use low horizontal timber slats between powder-coated metal posts along z -6 and x -6, around 0.85 m high and below 1.2 m. Leave the +z front open with a clear gate gap. Keep spacing open enough to see the build beyond.
rules.ownerMarker: Mount a clean, modest rectangular nameplate on the front post with an owner-colour strip in #d9534f and a filled circular household emblem. Print the exact player name in large, simple lettering. Avoid estate-agent branding, giant billboards or unnecessary illuminated screens.
rules.lighting: Street light: 12 parts at x 0, z 5. Use a slim powder-coated pole, short curved arm and flat LED head with a broad underside diffuser. Only the diffuser uses glow=true. The shape must read as contemporary street infrastructure rather than a gas lamp with a white bulb.
rules.centrepiece: Use 48 parts for a low circular civic fountain about 4.5 m across, with pale concrete coping, a shallow blue basin and three short water jets. Add a simple offset stone form rather than historic statuary. Recessed pool-light lenses use glow=true; water and jets do not. Keep the centre low, accessible and visibly distinct from the Industrial Age's tiered cast-iron fountain.
rules.seating: Use 12 parts for a two-person bench with broad timber slats, a simple aluminium frame and a shallow backrest. Seat height is about 0.45 m. Add one arm divider only if it does not reduce the clear two-person reading; avoid ornate iron ends.
rules.market: Use 32 parts within 2.6 × 1.6 m for a compact kiosk with a flat overhang, powder-coated panels, a glass display, a service hatch and visible fruit crates, pastries and refill bottles. Use clear blocks of colour and unbranded packaging. The stall is a little contemporary shop, not a medieval canopy with a cash register added.
rules.trees: Street pair: 30 parts total at x -3 and x 3, z 5; use a tall plane tree with a subtly bent trunk and a smaller maple with an uneven crown and one low branch. Place them in separate permeable tree pits, not matching circular planters. Wild group: 38 parts for a tall oak, a broad willow and a flowering shrub. Countryside dressing: 14 sparse low parts of meadow flowers, grass clumps, fallen twigs, rounded stones and occasional shallow rain puddles, mostly below 0.35 m. Municipal care never means identical trees.
rules.arrival: Use 64 parts for a bus stop and short city minibus. At z 5 place a narrow transparent shelter, small seat and pole with a large bus pictogram. At z 0, aligned along x, place a roughly 5 m minibus with a recognisable windscreen, side windows, rubber tyres and an opening-side door facing the stop. Keep the boarding route clear and do not let the shelter consume the full walking strip.
rules.crossing: Use 58 parts for a simple precast-concrete road bridge running along z, about 4 m wide, with shallow beams, modest concrete abutments and open metal rails. Its deck meets the banks about 1 m above water. Water runs along x across |z| <= 7; the river tile shows its central 12 m and the real bank landings continue to z ±7. Add natural reed pockets, stones and small rainwater outlets without litter or excessive civil-engineering clutter.
rules.camp: Use 82 parts for a tourist coach, two broad parasol shelters and one small check-in awning across the river. Include luggage, a cooler, folding tables, a route display and a portable gathering light whose diffuser uses glow=true. The separate tour-guide leader uses 36 parts including the base figure: a bright practical jacket, bucket hat, neck lanyard and walking shoes, carrying a folded map. A suitcase with distant destination stickers and a contrasting regional scarf communicate travel without stereotypes.
rules.people: Use 46 parts total for two residents at x -0.6 and x 0.6, retaining the base bodies. One wears a hoodie, cropped trousers, trainers and loose textured hair and carries a small potted plant; the other wears a work jacket, jeans, sturdy shoes and tied-back hair and carries a phone. Use distinct body-accessory silhouettes, everyday fabrics and no brand logos.
rules.head: The Mayor uses 38 parts including the base figure. Give them a smart contemporary suit, a broad civic sash, a simple town badge and distinctive neat hair. Carry oversized rounded ceremonial ribbon scissors beside a short ribbon loop. The sash and scissors establish the office; do not retain the Alderman's top hat or heavy brass chain.

materials: Fine-grained asphalt and pale cast concrete
Rubber tyres and restrained plastic fittings
Contemporary cotton, knitwear and weatherproof fabric
avoid: Gas lanterns, steam vehicles and Victorian civic ornament
Medieval market awnings reused without transformation
Bronze or Stone Age primitive markers
Hovering vehicles, holograms and emissive road grids
Brand logos, dense advertising and tiny unreadable text
Perfectly identical street trees and sterile all-concrete landscapes
Photorealistic cars, glass reflections or fine texture that fight the toy style
designDirection: Make a friendly present-day small town from clear contemporary forms, healthy planting and restrained civic graphics, rendered as bright low-poly toys from the 40° overhead camera. Preserve the 5×5 block plan, 16 m parcels, four community project lots and camp across the river beyond the east ring road, with every upgrade retaining its footprint and purpose. Replace industrial ornament with accessible public space, mass-produced components and recognisable everyday services rather than simply painting old assets white. A skyscraper becomes a stepped steel-and-concrete tower, a car becomes a compact hatchback, and a café becomes a glass-fronted espresso bar with a small service terrace. Keep traffic markings flat, colour accents purposeful and signs readable by silhouette before text.
